question: From which of the following epics did the Garadi folk dance of Puducherry originate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramayana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Garadi folk dance of Puducherry is inspired by the epic **Ramayana**.
 
• This traditional dance form is performed during the festivals and celebrations in Puducherry.
 
• Garadi dance is characterized by the use of sticks and intricate footwork, symbolizing the battle between good and evil.
 
• Dancers often wear colorful costumes and masks representing various characters from the Ramayana.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional music played on instruments such as drums and cymbals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ramayana** is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient Indian literature, the other being the Mahabharata.
 
• It narrates the life of Prince Rama, his exile, the abduction of his wife Sita by Ravana, and his eventual victory over Ravana.
 
• The Ramayana has significantly influenced the art, culture, and religious practices across India and Southeast Asia.
 
• Various forms of dance, drama, and art in India draw inspiration from the Ramayana, making it a vital part of the cultural heritage.
